evals.prompt: I just started a new session and need to catch up on what the team has been discussing. Check ccchat for any unread messages, show me what's been happening, and start monitoring for new messages.
evals.expected_output: Agent reads unread messages via chat-read.js, shows status, starts background watcher. Uses --quiet flag appropriately. Demonstrates the Quick Start flow.

assertions.name: uses_quiet_flag
assertions.description: Uses --quiet flag on chat-read for clean polling

assertions.name: starts_background_watcher
assertions.description: Sets up chat-watch.js as background process

assertions.name: checks_existing_watcher
assertions.description: Uses pgrep to check if watcher already running before spawning

assertions.name: shows_status
assertions.description: Runs status.js to show who's online

assertions.name: cursor_advancement_awareness
assertions.description: Explains that watcher does NOT advance read cursor and chat-read must follow

evals.prompt: I'm about to refactor the database layer in our project — it's a breaking change that will affect the API contract. I want to run this by the other agents before I start. Can you post about it in ccchat and get their input?
evals.expected_output: Agent sends a structured message about the breaking change. Should use --room general. Message invites critique with options and trade-offs, not just announces.

assertions.name: uses_correct_script
assertions.description: Uses chat-send.js or chat-ask.js to send the message

assertions.name: structured_message
assertions.description: Message includes problem statement and invites critique rather than just announcing

assertions.name: uses_correct_room
assertions.description: Targets --room general or an appropriate room

assertions.name: invites_debate
assertions.description: Message framing encourages genuine feedback, not just rubber-stamping

assertions.name: considers_blocking
assertions.description: Mentions chat-ask.js for blocking on responses or explains how to get replies

evals.prompt: There's an active plan in ccchat that I need to work on. Task #7 should be available for me to claim. Claim it, and then once I've implemented the change (I already ran the tests and they pass), mark it as complete.
evals.expected_output: Agent uses chat-claim.js to claim and complete. Flags evidence requirement. References workflow and review stages.

assertions.name: uses_complete_command
assertions.description: Uses chat-claim.js --complete 7 to mark task done

assertions.name: evidence_requirement
assertions.description: Flags that 'tests pass' alone is not sufficient evidence — must show actual output

assertions.name: workflow_awareness
assertions.description: References the task implementation workflow or its requirements

assertions.name: review_stages_awareness
assertions.description: Mentions that spec compliance and quality reviews are needed before task closes
